summary: Collect the sum of every contiguous subarray in a set with a double loop and a running sum, then count up from 1 until a number is missing (T12 — subarray sums). Because all numbers are positive, a running sum that grows too big can be cut off early.

blocks.title: Read the array
blocks.text: N on one line, the elements on the next, as `int`s. Do NOT sort — that changes which subarrays exist.

blocks.title: The answer can't be bigger than LIMIT
blocks.text: There are only N(N+1)/2 subarrays, so at most that many different sums. So among 1, 2, …, N(N+1)/2 + 1 at least one is missing, and the answer is ≤ `LIMIT`.

blocks.title: Store sums in a set
blocks.text: A set answers `ans in sums` instantly. A list would scan up to millions of items for every check.

blocks.title: Running sum for every start
blocks.text: For each start `i`, `s` grows by one element at a time, so `s` is always `sum(arr[i..j])` — no need to re-add the whole subarray each time.

blocks.title: Stop early when the sum is too big
blocks.text: All numbers are positive, so the running sum only grows. Once it passes `LIMIT` it can never be the answer, and neither can any longer subarray from this start, so we `break`.

blocks.title: Find the smallest missing number
blocks.text: Start at 1 and step up while the number is in the set. This always stops by `LIMIT`.

complexity: Time O(N²) with N ≤ 2000 → at most about 2 million additions (~0.35 s), usually far fewer thanks to the break.
pitfalls: Sorting the array — that solves a different (subset) problem.
Using a list instead of a set for the sums.
